chunks: By Allah, if I wished, I could inform every one of you of his origin, his destination, and all his affairs, and I would do so,
but I fear that you would disbelieve in the Messenger of Allah on my account.
Indeed, I shall convey it to the select few from whom that is trusted.
By the One who sent him with the Truth and chose him above creation, I do not speak except truthfully,
and He has charged me with all of that, and with the death of whoever perishes, the salvation of whoever is saved, and the final outcome of this matter,
and He left nothing that passes through my mind without pouring it into my ears and conveying it to me.

key_terms.أَفْرَغَهُ: he poured it out (conveyed it fully)

ai.seo_question: What does the Imam mean by conveying knowledge to the 'select few' and what is the source of his truthful speech?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) distinguishes between his absolute truthfulness (as affirmed by the Prophet's covenant) and the potential for disbelief (kufr) if he revealed all hidden secrets to the general public, a concept central to the Shia doctrine of 'Ilm al-Ghayb granted to the Imams. He clarifies that while he possesses complete knowledge of individual fates and the ultimate outcome of affairs, he selectively communicates this to those capable of bearing it, thereby preserving the people's faith in the Prophet's message.
